title: Renewal + staged expansion: proposed 16→32 GPU uplift and hourly reserved rates
text:
Renewal + staged expansion: proposed 16→32 GPU uplift and hourly reserved rates

['From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@tactico.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal + staged expansion: proposed 16→32 GPU uplift and hourly reserved rates

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the great conversation last week. Per our discussion, I attached a concise proposal that outlines a staged path to move Tactico from your current 16 reserved GPUs to 32 reserved GPUs at renewal. High-level summary:

- Staged rollout: add 16 GPUs in a canary / ramp phase (30 days) to validate throughput and cost before the full commit.
- Price construct: revised per-GPU reserved hourly rates for the 32-GPU commit, plus a short trial discount applied to the upsell tranche during the ramp.
- Throughput guarantees: we propose explicit throughput SLOs for the expanded pool and an SLA credit schedule if targets are missed.

Attachments: tactico-upgrade-proposal-20270322.pdf (proposal + pricing examples), throughput-sla-table-20270322.csv (detailed SLO targets and measurement windows).

Questions for you: does Tactico prefer a single annual commitment for the full 32 GPUs or a staged annual commit (16 base + 16 with a 60-day conversion window)? For next steps, I can schedule a 30-minute call with Lauren (technical lead) and Monica (renewals specialist) to walk the proposal on Tuesday or Thursday this week — what times work for you?

Thanks — I’ll keep the proposal flexible to your procurement window.

—Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0188
Redwood Inference

[attachment: tactico-upgrade-proposal-20270322.pdf]', 'From: Elena Ruiz <elena@tactico.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 12:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Renewal + staged expansion: proposed 16→32 GPU uplift and hourly reserved rates

Aditya —

Appreciate the proposal and the clarity. A few quick items from procurement and engineering after a rapid read-through:

- Need a clear per-hour, per-GPU number for the additional 16 GPUs during the ramp and for the committed state. Our CFO wants to model monthly spend precisely.
- We must see the throughput SLOs tied to a defined measurement window (how you calculate p95/p99 on a rolling 7/30d basis) — the CSV helps but please reiterate in the offer.
- Can we get a 30-day ramp where the add-on GPUs are billed at a discounted trial rate, and if we convert to the 32-GPU commit within that period we receive a blended retroactive credit to match the committed rate?

Also, procurement asks for target dates: we need the effective start date, proposed term length, and any early-termination fees or step-down schedule. Our renewal window is tight (we need signatures in the next 21 days).

If you can incorporate those specifics and share an updated one-page term sheet, I can run it by Marco (procurement) and the CFO. Otherwise we can do a call Wednesday afternoon.

—Elena Ruiz
Head of ML Ops, Tactico AI
elena@tactico.ai

[inline: please include per-hour math and sample month-by-month cost table]', "From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Renewal + staged expansion: proposed 16→32 GPU uplift and hourly reserved rates

Team — forwarding Elena's note. Key asks to incorporate into a revised one-page term sheet:

1) Clear per-GPU per-hour numbers for (a) trial/ramp 16 GPUs, (b) committed 32 GPUs (blended), and (c) retroactive credit mechanics if they convert inside the ramp window.
2) Explicit SLA/throughput measurement windows + credit schedule (they asked about rolling 7/30d).
3) Effective start date and term length (they need signatures inside 21 days).

My proposed structure to keep the deal moving and stay competitive:
- Current 16 GPUs: keep at existing agreed rate of $2.80/hr per GPU (no change).
- Additional 16 GPUs (ramp tranche): trial pricing at $1.65/hr per GPU for the first 30 days of the ramp. If Tactico signs to convert to a full 32-GPU annual commitment within 30 days, we apply a retroactive credit so the effective per-GPU blended rate across all 32 GPUs is $2.20/hr.
- If they convert after 30 days but within 60 days, the blended rate moves to $2.30/hr. No conversion after 90 days.
- Throughput SLOs: we propose measuring p95 latency over a rolling 7-day window and p99 over a rolling 30-day window; targets and credit thresholds are in throughput-sla-table-20270322.csv. SLA credit up to 10% of monthly committed fees for repeated miss.

Please confirm margin-side feasibility and whether we can offer a 30-day trial at $1.65/hr on the ramp GPUs. If that’s too aggressive, suggest the floor and an alternative conversion cadence we can present.

Thanks — I’ll prepare a one-page term sheet after alignment.

—Aditya (internal)

From: Elena Ruiz <elena@tactico.ai>
Subject: Re: Renewal + staged expansion: proposed 16→32 GPU uplift and hourly reserved rates

[quoted above]", 'From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal + staged expansion: proposed 16→32 GPU uplift and hourly reserved rates

Aditya —

Numbers look promotable but we should tighten the conversion windows and protect margin. My recommendation:

- Keep existing 16 GPUs at $2.80/hr.
- Ramp tranche (additional 16 GPUs): offer 45-day trial at $1.80/hr (instead of 30-day at $1.65). This gives the customer more runway; financially we recover a bit more.
- Conversion mechanics: if Tactico converts within the 45-day window, apply a retroactive blended credit to land the effective full-32 blended rate at $2.25/hr. If they convert after day 45 but before day 90, blended rate $2.35/hr. After 90 days, the ramp GPUs revert to on-demand rates (no retroactive credit).
- Term: 12-month commitment for the full 32 GPUs with a 60-day early-termination notice and a standard pro-rata termination fee (we’ll use the standard redemption language).
- SLA: tighten p95 measurement to rolling 7-day, include a 7-day cure period before credits trigger; escalate to engineering on repeated breaches.

Ben — can you run margin impact for the 45-day $1.80/hr trial and the eventual blended $2.25/hr? If it’s > 35% contribution margin we’re fine. If not, I’d push the trial to $1.95/hr.

If approved, I’ll draft the one-page term sheet and route for legal to add the standard SLA appendix and termination language.

—Monica
Director, Renewals Operations, Redwood Inference', 'From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@tactico.ai>, Marco Chen <procurement@tactico.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Mar 2027 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Revised offer: 16→32 GPU staged expansion — final term sheet and timing

Elena / Marco —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Per our internal alignment, attached is a short, binding term sheet summarizing the revised offer (see tactico-revised-offer-20270325.pdf). Key points below:

- Effective start date: 2027-04-01 (term runs 12 months from the effective start date).
- Pricing: existing 16 GPUs remain at $2.80/hr per GPU. The additional 16 GPUs are added as a ramp tranche with a 45-day discounted trial at $1.80/hr per GPU. If Tactico converts to a full 32-GPU annual commitment during the 45-day window, we apply a retroactive credit so the blended effective per-GPU rate across the 32 GPUs is $2.25/hr. If converted between day 46–90, blended rate is $2.35/hr.
- Measurement & SLA: p95 measured on a rolling 7-day window; p99 on a rolling 30-day window. We include a 7-day cure period; SLA credits up to 10% of monthly committed spend for repeated breaches. Detailed metrics and thresholds are in the attached SLA table.
- Procurement notes: standard 60-day early termination pro-ration and redemption schedule. DocuSign link to the term sheet is below.

DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/ABC123-tactico-upgrade
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234560/deal/HL-2027-TAC-0193

Next steps: if you’re good with the term sheet I’ll send the DocuSign envelope and schedule a technical onboarding call with Lauren next week to validate traffic pattern baseline for the canary pool. We’ll also provision monitoring hooks so SLA measurement is visible to your team from day one.

Looking forward to moving this across the finish line — happy to join a 30-minute call if you want to walk through the numbers.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0188
